RCW 9.95.240 has two limbs: subsection (1) permits a defendant who fulfilled probation, or was discharged early, to withdraw a guilty plea or have a verdict set aside and the charging document dismissed, at any time before the maximum period of punishment expires, in the court's discretion, with a proviso preserving the conviction for pleading and proof in any subsequent prosecution; subsection (2)(a) permits application after probation expires for vacation under RCW 9.94A.640, the court applying the equivalent of the RCW 9.94A.640(2) tests as they would apply to a person convicted of a crime committed before 1 July 1984, which fixes the scope as the pre-Sentencing Reform Act route. tracks.legalName: Petition to Vacate a Misdemeanour or Gross Misdemeanour Conviction, RCW 9.96.060(2)
tracks.publicName: Vacate a Washington misdemeanour conviction after three clean years

controllingAuthority.summary: Washington vacates; it does not expunge adult convictions. On a granted petition the court permits withdrawal of the guilty plea and entry of a not guilty plea, or sets aside the guilty verdict, then dismisses the charging document and vacates the judgment and sentence. The applicant must have completed all terms of sentence including satisfaction of financial obligations; at least three years must have passed since the later of release from supervision or probation, release from total and partial confinement as defined in RCW 9.94A.030, or the sentencing date; and there must be no new crime in this state, another state or federal or tribal court in the three years before the application. Since 2024 c 296 the three-year clock no longer restarts on the date legal financial obligations are paid off, and the court may be asked to cancel or reduce some of them. Relief is discretionary: the court may in its discretion vacate even where every requirement is met, which makes Washington unusual and means no outcome may be promised. On vacation the person is released from all penalties and disabilities, the conviction is not included in criminal history for later sentencing, and for all purposes including employment and housing the person may state they were never convicted.

exclusions: Any pending charge in Washington, another state, or federal or tribal court.
A violent offence as defined in RCW 9.94A.030, or an attempt.
DUI, physical control, railroad intoxication, or an RCW 46.61.5055 prior offence, subject to the ten-year rule.
Any misdemeanour or gross misdemeanour violation or attempt under chapter 9.68, chapter 9.68A or chapter 9A.44 RCW, except failure to register under RCW 9A.44.132.
Convictions meeting the RCW 9.96.060(2)(f) domestic violence conditions, which are the separate DV track.
The protection order conditions at RCW 9.96.060(2)(i).
Felony convictions, which run under RCW 9.94A.640.

waitingPeriods.duration: At least three years since the later of release from supervision or probation, release from total and partial confinement, or the sentencing date, RCW 9.96.060(2)(g).
No new crime in this state, another state, or federal or tribal court in the three years prior to the application, RCW 9.96.060(2)(h).

tracks.legalName: Petition to Vacate a Domestic Violence Misdemeanour or Gross Misdemeanour Conviction, RCW 9.96.060(2)(f)
tracks.publicName: Vacate a Washington domestic violence misdemeanour after five years

controllingAuthority.summary: The domestic violence branch of the misdemeanour vacation statute, separate because it has a different waiting period, an added notice requirement, a count limitation, an affidavit trap and a different legal effect. The DV trigger does not require a RCW 10.99.020 designation: the court may determine, after reviewing the court file and the totality of the records including any prior RCW 10.99.020 convictions or comparable out-of-state or federal offences and the damage to person or property, that the offence involved domestic violence, so an agent screening only for a DV tag will misroute. Four disqualifying factors each block relief: the applicant has not given written notification of the vacation petition to the prosecuting attorney's office that prosecuted the offence, or has not given that notification to the court; the applicant has two or more DV convictions stemming from different incidents, with the favourable rule that where the current application covers more than one conviction arising from a single incident none of those counts as a previous conviction; the applicant signed an affidavit under penalty of perjury affirming no previous DV conviction and a criminal history check reveals one; or less than five years have elapsed since completion of the terms of the original conditions of sentence including any ordered treatment but excluding payment of financial obligations. The distinct effect is valuable and concrete: on vacation the state may not use the conviction in a later prosecution except for violating a restraining, no-contact or protection order, stalking under RCW 9A.46.110, or a domestic violence or vulnerable adult protection order under chapter 7.105 RCW, and the vacated conviction is not a conviction of such an offence for the purposes of 27 C.F.R. 478.11.

exclusions: Two or more domestic violence convictions stemming from different incidents.
Any case where written notification has not been given both to the prosecuting attorney's office that prosecuted the offence and to the court.
Any case where less than five years have elapsed since completion of the original conditions of sentence including any ordered treatment.
The ordinary RCW 9.96.060(2) bars, which continue to apply.
Felony domestic violence convictions, which run under RCW 9.94A.640.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: Kept separate from the ordinary misdemeanour route exactly as the controlling review directs, because it differs on the waiting period, the notice requirement, the count limitation, the declaration risk and the legal effect. controllingAuthority.summary: A mandatory route reaching misdemeanour, gross misdemeanour and felony convictions alike, notwithstanding RCW 9.94A.640, which is broader than the internal reference's footnote treatment. It applies to a conviction before 1 January 1975 of violating any statute or rule regarding the regulation of fishing activities, including the enumerated former fisheries and game statutes, where the person claimed to be exercising a treaty Indian fishing right. The court must find two things: that the applicant is a member of a tribe that may exercise treaty Indian fishing rights at the location where the offence occurred; and that the state has been enjoined from enforcing the statute or rule to the extent it interferes with a treaty Indian fishing right as determined under United States v. Washington or Sohappy v. Smith and any post-trial orders, or any other state supreme court or federal court decision. On those findings the court shall vacate. The person may apply, or, if the person is deceased, a family member or an official representative of the tribe of which the person was a member may apply on their behalf.

exclusions: Any conviction on or after 1 January 1975.
Any conviction not for violating a statute or rule regulating fishing activities.
Any case where the person was not claiming to be exercising a treaty Indian fishing right.
Any case where the applicant is not, and the subject was not, a member of a tribe that may exercise treaty Indian fishing rights at the location of the offence.

tracks.publicName: Vacate a Washington class B or class C felony conviction

controllingAuthority.summary: Felony vacation in the sentencing superior court. The applicant generally must first have been discharged under RCW 9.94A.637, and the certificate of discharge is a separate process and the most common blocker. Class A felonies are not available on this route. A class B felony requires at least ten years since the later of release from community custody, release from full and partial confinement, or the sentencing date, and no new crime in this state, another state or federal court in the ten years before the application. A class C felony requires five years on the same three-event latest-of test with a five-year clean period, except that a class C felony described in RCW 46.61.502(6) or 46.61.504(6) is carved out of that rule by subsection (2)(f) and then barred outright by subsection (2)(g). The bars are pending charges in this state, another state or federal court; a violent offence as defined in RCW 9.94A.030 OR a crime against persons as defined in RCW 43.43.830, which are two different and separately encoded lists; and any felony described in RCW 46.61.502 or 46.61.504. Three narrow exceptions to the violent and person-crime bar exist, available only where the conviction did not include a firearm, deadly weapon or sexual motivation enhancement: assault in the second degree under RCW 9A.36.021; assault in the third degree under RCW 9A.36.031 when not committed against a law enforcement officer or peace officer; and robbery in the second degree under RCW 9A.56.210.

exclusions: Class A felonies.
Any pending charge in this state, another state or federal court.
A violent offence as defined in RCW 9.94A.030, subject only to the three narrow exceptions.
A crime against persons as defined in RCW 43.43.830, which is a separate and longer list from the violent offence list and must be encoded separately.
Any felony described in RCW 46.61.502 or RCW 46.61.504, including the class C felonies described in RCW 46.61.502(6) and 46.61.504(6).
Any conviction that included a firearm, deadly weapon or sexual motivation enhancement, which closes the three narrow exceptions.
Assault in the third degree committed against a law enforcement officer or peace officer, which the exception does not reach.

tracks.legalName: Dismissal After Probation and Vacation of a Pre-1984 Conviction, RCW 9.95.240
tracks.publicName: Clear an older Washington conviction after you finished probation

controllingAuthority.summary: Read at source on 2026-08-06, RCW 9.95.240 is one of only four routes RCW 9.94A.030(11)(b) recognises for removing a conviction from criminal history, and it has two distinct limbs. Subsection (1): every defendant who has fulfilled the conditions of probation for the entire period, or who was discharged from probation before the period ended, may at any time before the maximum period of punishment for the offence expires be permitted in the court's discretion to withdraw a guilty plea and enter a plea of not guilty, or, where convicted after a plea of not guilty, have the verdict set aside, and the court may then dismiss the information or indictment, after which the person is released from all penalties and disabilities resulting from the offence. The probationer is to be informed of this right in their probation papers. A proviso preserves the conviction for pleading and proof in any subsequent prosecution for any other offence, with the same effect as if probation had not been granted. Subsection (2)(a): after the period of probation has expired, the defendant may apply to the sentencing court for vacation of the record of conviction under RCW 9.94A.640, and the court may in its discretion clear the record if it finds the defendant has met the equivalent of the RCW 9.94A.640(2) tests as those tests would be applied to a person convicted of a crime committed before 1 July 1984. That fixes the scope the controlling review could not: this is the pre-Sentencing Reform Act route. Subsection (2)(b) carries the same clerk transmittal to the Washington State Patrol identification section and any local police agency, the same immediate-update and FBI transmittal duties, and the same bar on dissemination except to criminal justice enforcement agencies.

exclusions: On the subsection (1) limb, any application made after the maximum period of punishment for the offence has expired.
On the subsection (1) limb, any defendant who did not fulfil the conditions of probation for the entire period and was not discharged early.
On the subsection (2)(a) limb, any offence committed on or after 1 July 1984, for which RCW 9.94A.640 or RCW 9.96.060 applies directly.
Any expectation that the conviction disappears for later prosecutions: the subsection (1) proviso preserves it for pleading and proof in any subsequent prosecution for any other offence.

tracks.legalName: Request to Delete Non-Conviction Criminal History Record Information, RCW 10.97.060
tracks.publicName: Ask the Washington State Patrol to delete a record of a case that did not end in conviction

controllingAuthority.summary: The only real deletion mechanism in Washington, and it does not touch convictions. Non-conviction criminal history record information is subject to deletion from generally searched criminal justice agency files where two years or more have passed since a favourable disposition, or three years from arrest, citation or warrant for an offence where no conviction was obtained. The request goes to the Washington State Patrol rather than to a court: it is an agency request, not a petition. Two bars apply outright, the person being a fugitive and the case remaining under active prosecution. Beyond those the agency retains discretion to refuse on three common grounds: the disposition was a deferred prosecution or similar diversion; the person has a prior felony or gross misdemeanour conviction; or the person has been arrested for or charged with another crime during the intervening period. WashingtonLawHelp states directly that it is hard for information to qualify as non-conviction data under the rules, which makes deletion hard to obtain, and that expectation must be set before anyone pays. Where deletion is refused there is a fallback: RCW 10.97.040 requires agencies to check with the WSP for the most current and complete information before reporting a conviction, and RCW 10.97.110 supports a suit, potentially with attorney fees, against an agency that violates the requirement.

Any person who is a fugitive.

controllingAuthority.summary: Blake relief rests on the conviction being unconstitutionally void rather than on any waiting period or clean record. tracks.legalName: Application for a Certificate of Restoration of Opportunity, RCW 9.97.020
tracks.publicName: Get a Washington court certificate that stops most licensing bodies disqualifying you for your record

controllingAuthority.summary: Read at source on 2026-08-06. A certificate of restoration of opportunity is a court-issued instrument that operates on the collateral consequences of a conviction rather than on the record itself, and RCW 9.94A.030(11) treats issued certificates as part of the criminal history a sentencing court sees, which confirms it is a recognised instrument rather than an informal document. Its operative effect is at RCW 9.97.020(1): no state, county or municipal department, board, officer or agency authorised to assess the qualifications of an applicant for a licence, certificate of authority, qualification to engage in a profession or business, or admission to a qualifying examination may disqualify a qualified applicant solely on the basis of criminal history where the applicant holds a certificate and meets all other statutory and regulatory requirements, except as required by federal law or as exempted. The exemptions are extensive and must be encoded: criminal justice agencies as defined in RCW 10.97.030 and the Washington State Bar Association are exempt outright, and the section does not apply to the licensing, certification or qualification of accountants, bail bond agents, escrow agents, nursing home administrators, nursing, physicians and physician assistants, private investigators, receivers, teachers, notaries public, real estate brokers and salespersons, security guards, and vulnerable adult care providers who are not home care aides or contracted providers or licensees as defined in RCW 43.20A.715. The Department of Social and Health Services and its contracted providers and licensees retain sole discretion whether to consider a certificate when hiring or licensing for positions caring for or having unsupervised access to vulnerable adults or children. Nothing in the section restores or creates a means to restore firearm rights or eligibility for a firearm dealer licence under RCW 9.41.110, and nothing requires the removal of a protection order. Eligibility is set by the RCW 9.97.010(1) definition of qualified applicant, on a graduated scale: one year from sentencing for a misdemeanour or gross misdemeanour probation, deferred or other noncustodial sentence; eighteen months from release from confinement on such an offence; two years from sentencing, or from release from confinement, for a class B or C felony; and five years from sentencing, or from release, for a violent offence as defined in RCW 9.94A.030. The applicant must also be in compliance with or have completed all sentencing requirements, including having paid legal financial obligations in full, being fully compliant with a payment plan, or being out of compliance with a payment plan but having established good cause with the court. And the applicant must never have been convicted of a class A felony or an attempt, solicitation or conspiracy to commit one, a sex offence as defined in RCW 9.94A.030, a crime including sexual motivation under RCW 9.94A.835, RCW 13.40.135 or RCW 9.94A.535(3)(f), or extortion in the first degree, among the further bars in that subsection. The procedural half of the section was read at source on 2026-08-08 and is carried here. RCW 9.97.010(2) defines a qualified court as any Washington superior court in the county where the applicant resides or that sentenced or adjudicated them, and provides that where the sentencing or adjudicating court was a court of limited jurisdiction the qualified court is the superior court in the county of conviction or adjudication; a district or municipal court is therefore never itself a qualified court. RCW 9.97.020(2) gives a qualified court jurisdiction to issue a certificate to a qualified applicant, and RCW 9.97.020(2)(a) leaves it to that court's discretion whether the certificate applies to all past criminal history or only to the convictions or adjudications in the jurisdiction of the court. The application is filed as a civil action under RCW 9.97.020(7). Under RCW 9.97.020(6) the applicant must notify the prosecutor in the county where the certificate is sought, and must also notify the prosecuting attorney in any other jurisdiction that sentenced the applicant in the five years preceding the application; the prosecutor in the county of application supplies the court with a report of the applicant's criminal history. Under RCW 9.97.020(8) a superior court in the county in which the applicant resides may decline to consider the application, in which case it must dismiss without prejudice, state the reason on the order, and the applicant may refile in another qualified court, while the superior court in the county of the applicant's conviction or adjudication may not decline to consider the application; a court of either county that finds the applicant not qualified must likewise dismiss without prejudice and state the reasons on the order. The section provides no transfer procedure: the remedy for a declining court is dismissal and refiling by the applicant, not transfer by the court. Under RCW 9.97.020(9) the court decides without a hearing on the application and the prosecutor's pleadings unless it determines a hearing is necessary, and under RCW 9.97.020(10) the clerk of the granting court transmits the certificate to the Washington State Patrol identification section. RCW 9.97.020(11) directs the Administrative Office of the Courts to develop instructions, forms and an informational brochure, including at least a sample standard application and a form order, distributed to all county clerks and superior courts and translated into the state's significant non-English-speaking languages.

exclusions: Any person who has ever been convicted of a class A felony, or an attempt, criminal solicitation of, or criminal conspiracy to commit a class A felony.

Any person who has ever been convicted of a sex offence as defined in RCW 9.94A.030, or a crime that includes sexual motivation under RCW 9.94A.835, RCW 13.40.135 or RCW 9.94A.535(3)(f), or extortion in the first degree.
Any applicant who has not reached the applicable point on the RCW 9.97.010(1)(a) scale.

Any applicant not in compliance with sentencing requirements including legal financial obligations, unless on a compliant payment plan or with good cause established with the court for non-compliance.

geography.venue: A qualified court, and RCW 9.97.010(2) closes the set: a Washington superior court in the county where the applicant resides, or the superior court of the county that sentenced or adjudicated them. Where the sentencing or adjudicating court was a court of limited jurisdiction, the qualified court is the superior court of that county of conviction or adjudication; the district or municipal court that convicted the applicant is never itself a qualified court. Because the set is closed and statutory, one statewide packet serves the whole state as to venue and the county is a participant answer rather than a routing branch. The packet routes to the superior court of the county of the applicant's conviction or adjudication, because RCW 9.97.020(8) provides that court may not decline to consider the application.

destination.name: The superior court of a qualified county under RCW 9.97.010(2)
destination.detail: Filed as a civil action under RCW 9.97.020(7), at the superior court clerk's office of the chosen qualified county, with the notice to each prosecuting attorney RCW 9.97.020(6) requires. The packet routes to the superior court of the county of conviction or adjudication because RCW 9.97.020(8) provides that it may not decline to consider the application. The superior court of the county where the applicant resides remains statutorily available and may be nearer, and a participant who prefers it may use it, but that court may decline to consider the application; if it does, it must dismiss without prejudice, must state the reason on the order, and the applicant may refile in another qualified court. There is no statutory transfer procedure: the remedy is refiling by the applicant, not transfer by the court. Confirming intake with the clerk is prudent practice and not a legal prerequisite, and it is not a condition of generating this packet; which counties require additional accompanying documents under local superior court rules is a separate open filing-instruction question.

components.notes: Application for a certificate of restoration of opportunity under RCW 9.97.020, generated from the participant's answers: identity, the conviction history, the applicable point on the RCW 9.97.010(1)(a) scale with the dates it is computed from, the legal financial obligation compliance position, and a statement that none of the RCW 9.97.010(1)(c) bars applies. The Administrative Office of the Courts publishes a statewide pattern set under RCW 9.97.020(11), which has existed since 2016 and includes CRO 01.0100, Petition for Certificate of Restoration of Opportunity; the generated application conforms to it and states the qualified county the applicant is filing in. The strategy is custom_pleading and not official_pdf_fill because no CRO binary has been acquired, pinned or measured, there is no repository form identity to fill, and whether the CRO forms are mandatory, pattern or optional is an open build question belonging to the form-family owner. This memo does not guess it.

Proposed certificate and order prepared unsigned and undated for the judge, conforming to the Administrative Office of the Courts pattern CRO 01.0700, Order and Certificate of Restoration of Opportunity. CRO 01.0600, the Order of Dismissal, is the court's own order and is not a participant component.

The notice RCW 9.97.020(6) requires the applicant to give, prepared from the participant's answers, conforming to the Administrative Office of the Courts patterns CRO 01.0200, Notice of Filing a Petition, and CRO 01.0300, Proof of Service of that notice. The recipients are the prosecuting attorney of the county where the certificate is sought and, where any other jurisdiction sentenced the applicant in the five years preceding the application, the prosecuting attorney of that jurisdiction as well. The notice goes with the petition to the clerk at filing; the prosecutor of the county of application then supplies the court with a report of the applicant's criminal history.
Checklist naming the WSP criminal history record and the sentencing court docket, with what each costs and what each supplies.

Instructions covering what a certificate does and does not do, the graduated eligibility scale and which point applies, the legal financial obligation compliance options including the good-cause route, the exempt professions and bodies so that a participant is not sold a certificate that will not reach their licence, that firearm rights and protection orders are untouched, which superior courts are qualified and that the county of conviction or adjudication may not decline while the county of residence may, what a decline means in practice and that the remedy is refiling rather than transfer, that the application is filed as a civil action and the court may decide it without a hearing, that RCW 9.97.020(2)(a) leaves it to the court's discretion whether the certificate reaches all past criminal history or only the convictions in that court's own jurisdiction, that a filing fee applies and a GR 34 motion for a fee waiver is available to a participant who cannot pay it, and the local-rule check for additional accompanying documents.

rules.filing: File the application, the proposed certificate and order, and the notice package with the superior court clerk of a qualified county under RCW 9.97.010(2), as a civil action under RCW 9.97.020(7). The packet routes to the county of conviction or adjudication, whose superior court may not decline to consider the application under RCW 9.97.020(8). Confirming intake with the clerk is prudent practice, not a legal prerequisite, and not a condition of generation.
rules.fees: A superior court civil filing fee applies. The Administrative Office of the Courts' own instructions confirm that there is a filing fee and that a participant who cannot pay may ask for a waiver; they do not state the amount and none is asserted here, so the packet does not quote a figure and directs the participant to the clerk for it.
rules.feeWaiver: A participant who cannot afford the filing fee may ask the court for a waiver by GR 34 motion, which is the route the Administrative Office of the Courts' instructions name.
rules.notice: RCW 9.97.020(6): the applicant must notify the prosecutor of the county where the certificate is sought, and must also notify the prosecuting attorney of any other jurisdiction that sentenced the applicant in the five years preceding the application. The prosecutor of the county of application supplies the court with a report of the applicant's criminal history.
rules.service: The applicant sends the notice to each prosecuting attorney RCW 9.97.020(6) names and files proof of service with the petition; the Administrative Office of the Courts publishes CRO 01.0300 as the pattern proof of service and its instructions direct the applicant to bring the notices to the clerk with the petition.

selfHelpStopConditions: Any class A felony, sex offence, sexually motivated offence or first degree extortion conviction anywhere on the record.
The target licence or profession is one the section does not reach, in which case a certificate will not solve the participant's problem and they should be told so before paying.
The participant's real goal is firearm rights, which the section expressly does not restore.
There is a protection order the participant wants removed, which the section expressly does not require.

A residence-county superior court declines to consider the application. The dismissal is without prejudice, the order must state the reason and the applicant may refile in the county of conviction, but the stated reason may itself be the real problem and is worth reading with help.

Convictions in more than one county, because RCW 9.97.020(2)(a) leaves it to the court's discretion whether the certificate reaches all past criminal history or only the convictions in that court's own jurisdiction, and which county to file in is then a judgment about what the certificate will be worth.

venue.qualifiedCourt: Always a superior court. RCW 9.97.010(2) defines a qualified court as any Washington superior court in the county where the applicant resides or that has sentenced or adjudicated them.
venue.courtOfLimitedJurisdiction: Where the sentencing or adjudicating court was a court of limited jurisdiction, the qualified court is the superior court of that county of conviction or adjudication. A district or municipal court is never itself a qualified court, even where it is the court that convicted the applicant.
venue.permissibleCourts: At most two for any applicant: the superior court of the county of residence and the superior court of the county of conviction or adjudication. Where the applicant lives in the county of conviction the two coincide.
venue.jurisdiction: RCW 9.97.020(2) gives a qualified court jurisdiction to issue a certificate to a qualified applicant, so authorisation and subject-matter jurisdiction are coextensive on this route.
venue.declineRule: RCW 9.97.020(8). The superior court of the county in which the applicant resides may decline to consider the application; if it does it must dismiss without prejudice, must state the reason on the order, and the applicant may refile in another qualified court. The superior court of the county of the applicant's conviction or adjudication may not decline to consider the application. Dismissal for non-qualification is a different act available to either court, with the same without-prejudice consequence and a stated reason.
venue.transfer: None. The statute provides no transfer procedure. The remedy for a declining court is dismissal without prejudice and refiling by the applicant, so the packet must not tell a participant that their case will be moved for them.
venue.clerkConfirmation: Prudent practice, not a legal prerequisite. Nothing in RCW 9.97.010, RCW 9.97.020 or the Administrative Office of the Courts' instructions requires a participant to confirm anything with a clerk before filing, and the memo's previous design made generation contingent on an unverifiable participant step. Venue is now stated and the clerk check is an ordinary filing courtesy.
venue.packetRouting: The superior court of the county of conviction or adjudication, because it is the only venue the statute guarantees will be considered. The residence-county option is disclosed with its decline risk and the refiling remedy rather than hidden.
venue.oneStatewidePacket: Possible as to venue. The rule is statewide and closed, the county is a participant answer rather than a routing branch, and no county-specific variant is required.
venue.surveyDissolved: The memo's release blocker asked which superior courts have declined to consider certificate applications. It is retired by being dissolved rather than answered: routing to the court that may not decline makes the survey unnecessary. Which residence-county courts in fact decline is downgraded to a monitoring question.

form.finding: A complete statewide pattern set exists and has since 2016, published by the Administrative Office of the Courts under the RCW 9.97.020(11) duty: CRO 01.0100 Petition (rev. 12/2016), CRO 01.0200 Notice of Filing (rev. 06/2016), CRO 01.0300 Proof of Service (rev. 06/2016), CRO 01.0700 Order and Certificate (rev. 06/2016), with CRO 01.0600 Order of Dismissal as the court's own order, plus Instructions (rev. 01/2020) and a Brochure (12/2019), and static translations in Chinese, Korean, Russian, Spanish and Vietnamese. CRO 01.0600 is the court's dismissal order and is not a participant component. records_checklist and filing_instructions remain process guidance.
form.decision: custom_pleading, retained against official_pdf_fill. This is a decision and not a deferral: the generatable instrument today is a pleading that conforms to the pattern set. official_pdf_fill is unavailable because no CRO binary has been acquired, pinned or measured, no Washington source-materialization receipt exists for any of them, and there is therefore no repository form identity for a component to fill. It is also premature because whether the CRO forms are mandatory, pattern or optional is unresolved, and that answer decides whether a filer may lawfully substitute a conforming pleading at all.

RCW 9.97.020(11)(b) requires the instructions to include "a sample of a standard application and a form order", and the word sample points toward pattern rather than mandatory, but the Washington court rule governing the status of Administrative Office of the Courts forms was not read and no inference is drawn from the word alone. It belongs to the form-family owner.

certificateScopeDiscretion.rule: RCW 9.97.020(2)(a) leaves it to the issuing court's discretion whether the certificate applies to all of the applicant's past criminal history or only to the convictions or adjudications in the jurisdiction of that court.
certificateScopeDiscretion.participantConsequence: It bears on the venue choice in a way a participant should understand before choosing. Filing in the county of conviction guarantees the application is considered, but the certificate that court issues may be limited to that court's own convictions. A participant with convictions in several counties should be told this rather than left to discover it, and it is carried as a self-help stop condition and in the filing instructions.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: The controlling review recorded this as additional research required with the output strategy unresolved, and made it the first Washington research item after the two omitted vacation tracks on the ground that it is the answer to the largest ineligible population in the state. RCW 9.97.010 and RCW 9.97.020 are now read at source and the substance is determined: what a certificate is, that a court issues it, exactly what it does to licensing decisions, the long list of professions and bodies it does not reach, that it touches neither firearm rights nor protection orders, and a complete graduated eligibility scale with a legal financial obligation compliance element and a set of never-convicted bars. That is enough to import the track with a resolved strategy rather than defer it. What remains open is procedural rather than substantive: no pattern form was identified, so the strategy is custom_pleading; the fee and the notice mechanics were not established; and because the section permits certain superior courts to decline to consider applications, the receiving court is confirmed before filing. The exemption list is carried prominently and asked about at intake, because selling a certificate to someone whose target licence the section does not reach would take money for a document that cannot help them. [Amended by rcap-wa-crop-memo-amendment against the integrated rcap-wa-crop-venue-reconciliation decision. Two statements above are superseded and are kept only as the record of what the first pass concluded. First, "no pattern form was identified, so the strategy is custom_pleading": a complete statewide Certificate of Restoration of Opportunity pattern set exists and has since 2016, published by the Administrative Office of the Courts under the RCW 9.97.020(11) duty. The strategy remains custom_pleading, but for the opposite reason — the forms exist, none has been acquired, pinned or measured, there is no repository form identity to fill, and whether they are mandatory, pattern or optional is an open build question for the form-family owner. Second, "because the section permits certain superior courts to decline to consider applications, the receiving court is confirmed before filing": only the superior court of the county where the applicant resides may decline, and RCW 9.97.020(8) provides that the superior court of the county of conviction or adjudication may not. Venue is therefore stated rather than confirmed, clerk confirmation is prudent practice and not a legal prerequisite, and one statewide packet is possible as to venue. The full record is in _venueAndFormResolution.]
